subject: technology
lesson_title: Mastery check: adding a comment or suggestion
standards: Michigan Computer Science: Data and Analysis
essential_question: How can understanding productivity and collaboration tools help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery of adding a comment or suggestion through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of adding a comment or suggestion.
Check, revise, or improve work about adding a comment or suggestion using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about adding a comment or suggestion.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: This is day 5 of "Productivity and Collaboration Tools". That is unit 3 in grade 4. Today is a mastery demonstration about adding a comment or suggestion. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create an accessible one-page document or short slide set on a class topic. Today helps by working on adding a comment or suggestion. Your unit also covers efficient typing practice, formatting a document, building a simple slide, and using accessibility features. Today counts for a grade. Do it on your own.
primary_task: Show that you can do this on your own: adding a comment or suggestion. Put away the help sheet and the examples. Solve a new problem all the way. First write what answer you expect. Then test it two ways. Include one tricky case. Show what you expected and what you got. Then explain your thinking. Write it so someone new to adding a comment or suggestion could follow it. Everything you need is printed in activity_setup. It has the exact case, what should happen, how to try it, checks, and a paper choice worth the same score. Do not wait for another handout or app. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about adding a comment or suggestion. It is part of "Productivity and Collaboration Tools". Later days in this unit cover other things, like efficient typing practice. Before you stop, do this check: Rate confidence in adding a comment or suggestion, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. In grade 4, try the steps yourself before you ask for help. Give a reason in your own words for at least one choice. A labelled drawing or a spoken answer counts fully.

central_input.title: Inline design brief for adding a comment or suggestion
central_input.purpose: Design only for the fictional learner described here; no interview, public post, account, camera, or outside tester is needed.
central_input.fictional_user: Kai uses a keyboard, sometimes enlarges text to 200%, and wants a three-step way to track completed reading sessions without entering a name or location.
required_features: Add one reading session in at most three actions.
Show completion using both a word and a visual mark, not color alone.
Store only a fictional book label and a completed/not-completed value.
central_input.fixed_constraint: The prototype is a labelled paper sketch or local file; it is never published and collects no real personal data.

expected_behavior_and_specification: The response must apply adding a comment or suggestion to at least three labelled details from the supplied central input.
Every conclusion must identify the exact row, card, requirement, or scenario sentence that supports it.
The response must include one concrete revision or decision and explain the check that would show whether it worked.
The response must name one thing the supplied case does not tell you instead of guessing.

execution_method.primary: Paper-first method: copy the short labels, annotate them, and complete the response in a notebook or any notes app. No download, installation, account, or internet access is needed.
execution_method.local_optional: A locally available word processor, spreadsheet, drawing tool, or slide editor may be used, but no particular brand or paid feature is required.
execution_method.check_path: Use the numbered specification and the package test/check criteria as a checklist; a parent or tutor can verify the cited labels without needing subject software.

test_cases.expected: one stated check with an observable pass condition
one limitation, unknown, or trade-off stated without inventing facts

debugging_target.observed_failure: An unsupported answer names the lesson topic but cites no labelled detail and has no observable way to check the proposed change.
debugging_target.target: Replace unsupported claims with evidence-linked claims, then add one pass/fail check for the proposed revision or decision.
debugging_target.passing_change: A reader can trace every conclusion to a printed label in the central input and can perform the stated check without outside materials.

equal_credit_alternative.method: A handwritten, typed, spoken-to-a-scribe, or labelled-diagram response earns identical credit when it addresses the same specification.
steps: Label three facts from the central input.
Explain how each fact connects to adding a comment or suggestion.
State one revision or decision and its observable pass condition.
Name one limitation or missing fact without searching for outside information.
equal_credit_alternative.evidence_to_submit: Three labelled evidence links, the revision or decision, the pass condition, and the limitation or missing fact.

test_or_check_criteria: You solved it with no help sheet and no examples in front of you.
You wrote what you expected first, then tested two ways including a tricky one.
Someone new to this could follow your explanation.
This is your own work. Nobody did a graded part for you.
No real password, real person, or real website appears anywhere.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can do this with the keyboard only, no mouse needed. Text can be made bigger, and you may do it on paper instead of a screen.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, API key, or identifiable image.
Use only fictional or sandboxed systems, accounts, and data; never probe, exploit, or attempt to access a real external system.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.
The tutor may explain, demonstrate, or debug alongside the learner, but must not silently complete a graded project or assessment for them.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting adding a comment or suggestion.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for adding a comment or suggestion follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for adding a comment or suggestion, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for adding a comment or suggestion works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of adding a comment or suggestion, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking adding a comment or suggestion mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply adding a comment or suggestion under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on adding a comment or suggestion rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
